summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1967–1968) and the University of Munich (1968–1973), later holding posts at Munich (c. 1979–1993) and Göttingen (c. 1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He taught Jitendra Nath Banerjea and served as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture (and later History) at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1939 and 1965.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a linguist and Indologist. His career includes serving as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

Hendrik Arent Hamaker was a linguist who studied at the Athenaeum Illustre of Amsterdam (c. 1805–1815). He was a professor at the University of Franeker (1815–1817) and Leiden University (1817; 1822–1835), teaching Antonie Rutgers and Theodorus Willem Juynboll.
Hendrik van Gelder was an historian and archaeologist. He held academic posts at Utrecht University from 1906 to 1915 and at Leiden University from 1915 to 1921.

Henepola Gunaratana studied under Kiribatkumbure Sonuttara and Alagoda Sumanatissa, and at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, Kelaniya, and American University. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he led the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur and held posts at Georgetown and American University.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua. He held professorships at Dharma Realm Buddhist University, Graduate Theological Union, and Bond University.
Heng Yin works in Buddhist and religious studies. They completed a doctoral degree at Yunnan University (2018–2025) and held a post as Assistant Professor at China West Normal University in 2023.

Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1987–1997), later serving there as a postdoctoral researcher (1993–1997) and lecturer (2002–2008), as well as at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He held faculty posts at Utrecht University (assistant professor from 1966, chair of Sanskrit 1976–1992) and Leiden University (c. 1971–1976; professor 1992–2002).

Henri Arvon was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Strasbourg (c. 1934–1938). He taught at Prytanée National Militaire (c. 1945–1956), the University of Clermont-Ferrand (1966–1971), and Paris Nanterre University (c. 1965–1982).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, the École Normale Supérieure (c. 1878–1881), and the University of Paris (c. 1888–1889). He taught at Lycée David d'Angers (c. 1881–1883) and held a post at the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He served as librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society North China Branch (1871) and held professorships at Sciences Po (c. 1886–1925) and INALCO (from 1888).

Henri Deydier worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Przyluski, Henri Maspero, and Alfred Foucher, and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1945–1950), before taking a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 1950.

Henri Frei was a linguist and Japanologist who studied at INALCO, under Manu Leumann, and at the University of Geneva under Charles Bally. He held posts at Peking University (1933–1934), Maison Franco-Japonaise (c. 1934–1938), and Geneva (1940–1969).

Henri Gaidoz was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber. He taught at the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1876.
Henri Hauvette studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He subsequently held academic posts at Grenoble Alpes University from c. 1895 to 1908 and at the University of Paris from c. 1908 to 1935.

Henri Hubert studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. He held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (c. 1898–1927), the École du Louvre (1906), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1907).

Henri Maspero studied at INALCO and under Édouard Chavannes and Sylvain Lévi. A scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and religious studies, he held posts at EFEO (1908–1920), Collège de France (1919–1944), EPHE (c. 1932–1944), and the University of Paris (c. 1934–1944).

Henri Massé was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Algiers from c. 1916 to 1927 and at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes from c. 1927 to 1958.
